scope: 2021 first-printing multiplayer base game, including first/later setup and Chronicle; excludes Clockwork Prince and expansions
independence: Read the summary snapshot and authoritative Law, Playbook, supplied official errata, and both rendered reference.pdf pages. Did not read questions, keys, readers, grades, or other QA evidence.

sources_reviewed.coverage: All multiplayer core sections 1–10 and index; October 20, 2020
Core material pp. 2–32, including first-game diagrams, walkthrough and later-game setup; automated-opponent insert excluded
Both image-only pages rendered and visually inspected; p. 1 Card Reference and p. 2 Site Reference/Campaign Summary
Original first-game setup diagram visually checked

findings.claim: Homeland requires that no card has been discarded at the site this turn; its listed rewards omit gaining a secret.
findings.problem: The exclusion is only for a card OF THE HOMELAND SUIT discarded at that site. Discarding a different-suit card does not stop the Homeland reward. The Site Reference also explicitly includes gaining a secret among the printed Homeland rewards.
source_references: reference.pdf p. 2, Homeland Sites: "you have not discarded a card here of this suit during this turn"; the reward list begins with the gain-secret icon
findings.suggested_correction: Say no matching-suit card has been discarded there this turn, and include the printed secret reward.

findings.claim: A Homeland relic Recover still pays the normal relic cost but no Supply.
findings.problem: The higher-priority Site Reference directly instructs the player to take the relic, treating this as recovering it. It does not instruct them to perform the Recover action or pay the site resource cost. The summary adds a resource payment not present in the site power.
source_references: reference.pdf p. 2, Homeland Sites: "take the relic here, treating this as recovering it"
Law §9.1: the Site Reference is excepted from the normal Law-over-aids hierarchy
Playbook p. 27 describes Wastes as recovering its relic spending 0 Supply
findings.suggested_correction: Describe the power as taking the relic as a recovery, with no Supply or resource payment, rather than importing the ordinary Recover action cost.

findings.claim: Tribunal permits binding exchanges of favor, secrets, relics and banners.
findings.problem: The Site Reference permits immediate binding exchange of favor and secrets, plus binding future actions and combinations/penalties. It does not permit an immediate free relic/banner exchange. Adding those objects enables transfers that the source never authorizes.
source_references: reference.pdf p. 2, The Tribunal: "negotiate a binding exchange of [favor] and [secrets] as well as binding actions at any future time"
Law §7.6.3: players can promise to do the things the power lists
Law §9.1: do not infer unwritten rules
findings.suggested_correction: Limit its direct exchanges to favor and secrets; preserve the separately described future actions and penalties.

findings.claim: Attacker and then defender choose their ruled battle plans; no attacker/defender color restriction is explained anywhere.
findings.problem: The summary omits the red, blue and gradient battle-plan box permissions. Rule alone does not authorize every plan: red plans are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. This affects which plans can legally be used in the otherwise complete Campaign procedure.
source_references: Law §7.5 introductory paragraph: red, blue and gradient boxes indicate attacker, defender or either respectively
Playbook p. 14 battle-plan anatomy identifies the three power-box colors
findings.suggested_correction: Add the color permission mapping and say each side uses only eligible ruled plans.

findings.claim: The summary uses enemy-dependent site/card rules but never defines which players are enemies.
findings.problem: It explains that bandits are everyone's enemies but omits that normal Imperial players are not enemies of one another, while Exiles and temporarily non-Imperial Citizens consider other players enemies. This matters particularly for the quoted Shrouded Wood rule and enemy-restricted card powers.
source_references: Law p. 11, Glossary Enemy and Your Enemy
findings.suggested_correction: Add the Enemy/Your Enemy definitions, including the temporary Campaign exceptions.

findings.problem: This can be read as allowing an elective one- or two-card Search. The basic instruction is to draw three, reduced only by source exhaustion, world-deck Vision stopping, and applicable modifiers such as Marshes.
source_references: Playbook p. 32: draw three unless world Vision or no cards remain
findings.suggested_correction: Say draw three cards subject to the specified stop/reduction rules.

Saved map/boards, bank quantities at 5–6 players, Chancellor deployment/title/banner, Citizen starting warbands/no relic, site prompts, randomized Reliquary positions, deck segmentation, bottom draws and pawn placement checked against Law §1, Playbook p. 30 and errata §1.17. No material discrepancy found.

Mandatory order, Mob repetition and last-favor handling, Exile check-before-flip, opportunity sites, Supply spending/refresh/saving and Citizen exact-marker refresh checked against Law §4, board diagrams and errata §4.3.3. No material discrepancy found.

Source choice/cost, world-Vision stopping/counting, discard-before-play, site favor/capacity, advisers/true Visions, facedown play, destinations and resource cleanup, Conspiracy qualification and seizure penalty checked against Law §5.1, glossary, reference p. 1 and Playbook pp. 12, 27, 32. See F06 for draw-count wording.

Costs, empty-card requirement, eligible card types, matching-adviser yields, component exhaustion, relic access/cost, banner outbids/distribution/seizure and corrected Darkest Secret protection checked against Law §§5.2–5.4, §9.3 and supplied errata. No material discrepancy found in the ordinary actions.

Defender/local and remote target legality, pools/title bonus, side order, attack-pool removal, force composition, shields-only doubling, skull timing, exact sacrifice, ties, casualties, Imperial loss destinations, zero-garrison victory, seizure/banishment, end-plan timing and delayed Supremacy transfer checked against Law §5.5 and supplied errata. Automatic Chancellor, eligible/consenting Citizen Allies, shared modifiers/title bonus, own-adviser restriction, one user/payment per plan, side-wide pronouns versus own site/board, declared-defender priority and intra-Empire status checked against Law §§5.5, 6.6.3 and supplied errata. No material discrepancy found.

Travel matrix, reveal stocking, fixed/modifier/no-Supply order, facedown-adviser play, peeking history/Scepter restriction, warband transfers/last garrison, Scepter offers/exiling/self-exile costs, warband replacement, Act endings and full Supply checked against Law §§5.6, 6, 7.6.2, supplied errata and board text. No material discrepancy found.

Four Oath and Vision criteria, title ties/reset, shared Imperial site rule, strict Vision most, 3-Visions threshold, Wake timing, stable-regime rounds/rolls, successor substitution and exact round-8 priority checked against Law §§2.11, 3 and errata §3.2. No material discrepancy found.

Access/persistence, costs/exhaustion, out-of-turn payment, facedown secrets, restrictions/locks, adviser-limit errata, modifier timing/use, When Played order, hierarchy, finite components, private/public information, no extra loss and binding promises checked against Law §§7, 9–10, errata and reference p. 1. See F04–F05 for omissions.

Both reference pages visually checked. Opportunity, Coasts, Plains/Mountain, River, Charming Valley, Shrouded Wood, Narrow Pass, Great Slum, Marshes, Buried Giant, Hidden Place and Bandit Crown otherwise agree with their sources. See F01–F03 and F05.

Vision-alone Oath selection, Exile reset/other-player offers, one-garrison conversion, Imperial build/repair, map retention/ruins, exact repacking order, 3/2/1 additions and healing, 6 random dispossessions, relic ordering/refill, saved boards/map and corrected 12+18+remainder world deck checked against Law §8, supplied errata and Playbook pp. 4, 29–30. No material discrepancy found.
